questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belgium?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belgium article.

questions.proof: Its capital, Brussels, is the home of many organizations, including the European Union and NATO.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belgium?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belgium on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belgium article.

questions.proof: Belgium is bordered by the Netherlands in the north, Germany to the east, Luxembourg to the southeast and France to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Belgium?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Regions” part of the Belgium article.

questions.proof: Most of the people in this region, called the Flemish people, speak Dutch.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Adding back the Low Countries formed the United Kingdom of the _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Belgium article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Adding back the Low Countries formed the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Belgium is next to France, _____, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “France”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Belgium article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: Belgium is next to France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.
